sourceScript.version: Production script v1 — Research draft, not approved for narration

findings.claim: Eyes, ears and nostrils are positioned high on the head; nostrils can close underwater.
findings.source: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Nile Crocodile Fact Sheet — Physical Characteristics
findings.editorialNote: Use accurate close-up footage; do not suggest that the crocodile is fully invisible.

findings.claim: The tail provides the main forward thrust when swimming.
findings.source: San Diego Zoo Wildlife Alliance Nile Crocodile Fact Sheet — Behavior & Ecology
findings.editorialNote: Describe swimming footage only when the footage actually shows swimming.

findings.claim: Diet changes with age; juveniles eat insects and small fish, while adults take a broad range of prey and carrion.
findings.source: IUCN Crocodile Specialist Group — Crocodylus niloticus species account
findings.editorialNote: Avoid implying that every individual eats every listed prey type.

findings.claim: Females nest in sandy soil on elevated riverbank sites; nesting and parental care are part of the species' reproductive biology.
findings.source: IUCN Crocodile Specialist Group — Crocodylus niloticus species account
findings.editorialNote: Do not simulate nesting, hatching or maternal behaviour if authentic footage is unavailable.

findings.source: USGS Nonindigenous Aquatic Species — Nile Crocodile Species Profile
findings.editorialNote: The draft's general wording is acceptable; avoid oversimplifying temperature ranges or suggesting one universal threshold.

findings.claim: The species is globally Least Concern, while the South African regional assessment is Vulnerable.

sources.name: IUCN Crocodile Specialist Group — species account
sources.note: Global Least Concern assessment; CSG page identifies the global assessment as Least Concern.

sources.name: SANBI, 2023 SURICATA 10 regional assessment
sources.note: South African regional Vulnerable A2ac; the assessment rationale cites a decline exceeding 30% over three generations.

findings.editorialNote: Keep global and South African regional categories explicitly separate, as the draft currently does.

findings.claim: Nile crocodiles occupy rivers, lakes, wetlands and other suitable aquatic habitats across much of sub-Saharan Africa.
findings.source: IUCN Crocodile Specialist Group — Crocodylus niloticus species account
findings.editorialNote: Location-specific statements still require provenance for the actual footage.

editorialCorrectionsRecommended.currentWording: one of Africa's most powerful predators
editorialCorrectionsRecommended.recommendation: Consider 'one of Africa's largest aquatic predators' to avoid an imprecise superlative.

Do not describe the Pexels candidate as underwater, hunting, attacking, swimming or showing a particular behaviour until its original MP4 has been inspected. Its source-page description says it depicts a crocodile basking on a riverbank.
